mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-16.3 to -12.0), indicating an established recovery trend in shopping and leisure footfall that will persist and push the 4-week mean higher than the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior 3-week monotonic improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in TRANSIT from -50.7 to -45.6 signals renewed use of public transport for errands and commuting, which precedes and drives an increase in retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 4 points week-on-week, crossing above -46
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT moved from -50.7 to -45.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines in the two weeks following a TRANSIT jump exceeding 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility rises (commuting resumes) while RESIDENTIAL mobility simultaneously falls (less staying at home), the combined behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity drives a sustained increase in RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES rose from -20.6 to -13.7 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.1 to 5.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 4 weeks despite concurrent WORKPLACES rise and RESIDENTIAL decline in the base period.

mechanism_narrative: In a summer reopening regime, sustained elevated PARKS mobility reflects outdoor leisure substitution that co-occurs with rising RETAIL_REC as both are driven by warm-weather discretionary outings, so persistence of high PARKS values predicts continued RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS value was -25.7 and -27.7 in the last two weeks, well above the -32.4 trough three weeks ago
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 4 weeks even though PARKS stays above -30 for the two preceding weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility below the recent plateau indicates households spending less time at home, which translates into higher discretionary retail visits within one week as people redirect freed-up time to shopping and leisure.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls more than 1 point week-on-week, below 6.0
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.1 to 5.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL drop exceeding 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: A large single-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility (from -20.6 to -13.7) signals a policy-driven easing of restrictions on office attendance, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation activity within two weeks as workers resume in-person commerce near workplaces.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES jumped 6.9 points in the latest week after two weeks of decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no increase within two weeks of a WORKPLACES jump exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over two consecutive weeks reflects a broad-based normalization of daily mobility routines, which compounds to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the subsequent four weeks beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve in the same week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over 4 weeks is no larger than growth predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual rise in GROCERY_PHARM mobility from near-zero to positive territory signals a baseline normalization of essential errand activity that typically precedes a parallel uptick in discretionary retail visits within one week as overall out-of-home comfort increases.
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM rose from 1.3 to 4.7 over the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM.
